name: Distance to Proxima Centauri, 4.2465 ly (Gaia DR3 parallax inverted; IAU light year)

source.located: Gaia DR3 astrometry for Proxima Cen (Gaia EDR3/DR3 source_id 5853498713190525696). The catalogue is a database, not a paper; its entry was READ as printed in Reyle et al. 2021, arXiv:2104.14972 Table 1 (PARALLAX_BIBCODE 2020yCat.1350 = Gaia EDR3), and again as the 'Gaia DR3 value' column of Libralato, Bedin & Burgasser 2025, arXiv:2512.08533 Table 2. DR3 = EDR3 astrometry READ in Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2022, arXiv:2208.00211 (abstract; Sec. 3; Sec. 3.2-3.3). Zero-point READ in Lindegren et al. 2021, arXiv:2012.01742 (Sec. 2.2-2.3, Tables 9-10, Sec. 8, App. A). IAU light-year / au / parsec definitions NAMED-NOT-READ (IAU 2012 B2, 2015 B2); used only as the exact constants the tree already carries, and the tree's LY = c x Julian year was checked exactly.
source.via: Catalogue value restated verbatim (full digits) in 2104.14972 Table 1: PARALLAX 768.066539187357 mas, PARALLAX_ERROR 0.049872905 mas, EPOCH 2016.0, G 8.984749, BP 11.373116, RP 7.5685353, RV -22.345 km/s; 2512.08533 Table 2: 'Gaia DR3 value 768.067 +0.050/-0.050 mas'. 2208.00211 READ directly for the DR3=EDR3 identity and systematics.

published_statement: Gaia EDR3 (= DR3) parallax of Proxima Centauri: 768.066539187357 +- 0.049872905 mas at epoch J2016.0 (2104.14972 Table 1; 2512.08533 Table 2 '768.067 +- 0.050'). 2208.00211 abstract: 'The Gaia DR3 catalogue contains the same source list, celestial positions, proper motions, parallaxes, and broad band photometry ... already present in the Early Third Data Release, Gaia EDR3'; Sec. 3.2: 'the astrometry in Gaia DR3 is unchanged from Gaia EDR3'; Sec. 2: 'based on data collected over a 34-month time interval'; Sec. 3.3: 'the global parallax bias for Gaia DR3, as measured from quasars, is -17 uas ... varies as a function of magnitude, colour, and celestial position ... a recipe for correcting the parallaxes is given [L21]'. L21 Sec. 8: the bias function 'should be subtracted from the value (parallax) given in the Archive' -- i.e. the catalogue parallax is UNcorrected; 'Beyond the non-clamped interval 1.72 > nu_eff > 1.24 um^-1 (corresponding to 0.15 < GBP-GRP < 3.0) all results are in any case quite uncertain'. The distance 4.2465 ly is NOT a published statement of any source read: it is the tree's inversion 1/parallax, which re-derives to 4.2464599 ly (J2016.0).
published_hypotheses: H1 (measurement model): five- or six-parameter astrometric solution under the standard model of uniform linear barycentric motion, fitted to 34 months of Gaia data (2208.00211 Sec. 2-3); the solution type for Proxima was not READ.
H2 (epoch/frame): position and parallax at reference epoch J2016.0 (TCB), Gaia-CRF3 aligned to ICRF3 (2208.00211 Sec. 3.2; 2104.14972 Table 1 EPOCH 2016.0).

H3 (systematics): catalogue parallaxes carry an uncorrected zero-point bias (global QSO median -17 uas) depending on G, colour and ecliptic latitude, plus small-scale angular covariances ~26 uas RMS (2208.00211 Sec. 3.3; L21).
H4 (zero-point validity): the L21 recipe is 'provisional and indicative', and 'quite uncertain' outside 1.24 < nu_eff < 1.72 um^-1 (L21 Sec. 2.2, Sec. 8).
H5 (formal error): the published uncertainty 0.0499 mas is the formal catalogue error.

H6 (distance): distance = 1/parallax is the tree's step; it is safe when sigma/plx << 1 (here 6.5e-5, inversion bias ~4e-9) -- the GCNS (2012.02061) instead reports Bayesian posteriors, which at this precision coincide.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED uncertainty -- foliation.py:583 'PROXIMA_LY = 4.2465' and nonstatic.py:257 carry no error; the formal sigma is 0.0499 mas = 6.49e-5 relative = +-0.00028 ly = +-2.6e12 m, so the 5th significant figure the tree prints is uncertain (1-sigma interval 4.24618-4.24674 ly).

DROPPED epoch J2016.0 -- nonstatic.py:257 '# ly, Gaia DR3 parallax distance', ledger.py:333 '# ly, Gaia DR3 parallax' state the distance without epoch; with RV -22.345 km/s (2104.14972 Table 1) Proxima has approached by 7.6e12 m (-1.89e-4 relative, ~2.9 formal sigma) between J2016.0 and 2026.74: 4.24646 -> 4.24566 ly. The tree's 4.2465 is a J2016.0 value; at 5 s.f. today's value is 4.2457.

DROPPED zero-point -- the tree inverts the raw catalogue parallax (nonstatic.py:257; foliation.py:583). L21 says the bias should be subtracted, but Proxima (BP-RP = 3.80, nu_eff ~1.19 by L21 Eq. 1) lies outside the recipe's validity range; evaluated anyway as an illustration, Z5 = -37.9 uas and Z6 = -22.3 uas give -4.9e-5 and -2.9e-5 relative (4.2463 ly at 5 s.f.). Illustrative only, not a correction.

PRECISION beyond the datum (not an error) -- driven.py:772 checks the span 4.017499195e16 m to 1e-9, foliation.py:999 likewise, nonstatic.py:681-684 prints band time 17.909799392 d and crossing 2.123250000 yr, branelink.py:64-65 prints 'Proxima light time 134009348.4 s = 4.2465 yr EXACTLY (a light year is c times a Julian year)'. As arithmetic on the input all of these re-derive exactly, and branelink's parenthesis says truthfully that the exactness belongs to the unit definition. As physics they carry ~4 significant figures (6.5e-5 relative).

PRECISION -- ledger.py:2977 'the Proxima demand is 5.4194e42 kg to 5 figures': this re-derives (5.41940e42), but the formal parallax sigma moves it to 5.41905e42 / 5.41975e42, so the 5th figure is arithmetic reproducibility, not a physical figure.

ADDED (tree modelling, not in any source) -- driven.py:445-457 'corridor span = Proxima distance'. Measured: the heliocentric-vs-barycentric origin offset (1 au) is 3.7e-6 relative, below the formal sigma, so this choice is immaterial at the stated precision.

rederivation.outcome: 0 failures (exit 0). Reads the tree's constants read-only by regex. (1) LY = c x Julian year exactly; YR = Julian year; foliation and nonstatic carry the same 4.2465. (2) 1000/768.066539187357 mas = 1.301970531 pc = 4.246459923 ly, which rounds to 4.2465 (residual -4.0e-5 ly, inside the rounding half-unit). (3) Formal sigma 6.49e-5 relative = 0.000276 ly; the 1-sigma interval 4.24618-4.24674 spans several 5th-digit values; the inversion bias (~4e-9) is negligible. (4) Proxima's nu_eff ~1.19 < 1.24, outside L21 validity; illustrative Z5 -37.9 uas / Z6 -22.3 uas shift -4.9e-5 / -2.9e-5 relative. (5) DR2 gives 4.2439 ly, so 'DR3' is the discriminating attribution; HST agrees within 2 sigma. (6) Epoch drift to 2026.74 is -1.89e-4 relative (> formal sigma); the 1-au origin offset is 3.7e-6 (< sigma). (7) Every downstream figure re-derives exactly from 4.2465: span 4.0174991952e16 m, E = 2.7207442886e13 Msun, crossing 2.12325 yr, band 17.909799392 d, light time 134009348.400 s, exchange rate 1.3489476e26 kg/m, B2 5.41940e42 kg. (8) The largest moved or contested datum (DR2 -> DR3, 6.0e-4 relative) shifts log10 figures by 2.6e-4 orders (throatmass 48.92 unchanged at 2 dp); the 5th figure of 5.4194e42 is not fixed by the datum.

later_literature.ref: Libralato, Bedin & Burgasser 2025, arXiv:2512.08533 (A&A), ARES I
later_literature.what: HST WFC3 multi-epoch 2012-2025 astrometry of Proxima, tied to Gaia DR3 via L21-corrected field stars (Proxima excluded): parallax 768.373 +0.194/-0.162 mas against DR3 768.067 +- 0.050, reported agreement 1.19 sigma (0.5 sigma with chromatic terms). The authors state this is 'an independent test for the Gaia's astrometry of this very-red M dwarf' and find no colour-dependent discrepancy. It also records that excluding the microlensing epochs moved the HST parallax at ~2 sigma.

later_literature.ref: Ding et al. 2026, arXiv:2605.31402 (MNRAS preprint), refining the Gaia DR3 parallax zero-point
later_literature.what: Finds prominent local zero-point structure left after the L21 correction and builds a hybrid L21 + sliding-window map. Residual biases at the few-uas level (globular clusters -12 to +6 uas). No Proxima-specific value; the bright/red regime stays hardest to calibrate.
The catalogue parallax is biased; the bias is to be subtracted by the user; the recipe is 'quite uncertain' for nu_eff < 1.24 (Proxima ~1.19).
Earlier datum: Gaia DR2 parallax 768.529 +- 0.220 mas (zero-point corrected), J2015.5; DR3 moved it by -0.46 mas (2.05 combined sigma). A moved datum, not a refutation.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis -- that earlier workers lacked data -- tested for this result. What DR3 had: 34 months of Gaia data (2208.00211 Sec. 2), no extended mission, and a parallax zero-point calibrated only for 1.24 < nu_eff < 1.72 (L21), a range Proxima lies outside. What came later: (a) an independent 13-year HST parallax (2512.08533), 768.373/768.240 mas, agreeing within 1.2-1.7 sigma, which directly tests the colour-systematic worry for this very red star and finds none; (b) refined zero-point maps (2605.31402) that change bright-star corrections by a few uas; (c) Gaia DR4 (66 months, expected precision gain x1.4 per 2208.00211 Sec. 14) has not been READ here. Evidence either way: the datum DID move once with more data (DR2 -> DR3, -0.46 mas, 6e-4 relative, 2 sigma of DR2), so M's premise holds historically at the 4th significant figure. For a later release to move any conclusion of the tree it would have to move the parallax by a sizeable fraction of itself (the tree's conclusions are order-of-magnitude: 2.72e13 Msun, 48.92 orders, 5.42e42 kg). Every independent measurement READ here agrees to <= 6e-4 relative. Missing data therefore does not change the conclusion; it changes only the 4th-5th figures the tree prints. What the tree itself lacks is not data but hypotheses the data carry (sigma, epoch J2016.0, zero-point).
grade_evidence: The measurement stands. 1/parallax(DR3) = 4.2464599 ly (J2016.0), which rounds to the tree's 4.2465; every downstream figure re-derives exactly (script exit 0); every later datum READ (HST 2025, DR2, zero-point work) agrees to <= 6e-4 relative, and no moved or contested datum moves any downstream conclusion (worst log10 shift 2.6e-4 orders). It is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree drops three hypotheses the datum carries, each measured here. (i) The formal uncertainty is +-0.00028 ly, so the 5th figure (4.2465) and the '5 figures' of ledger.py:2977's 5.4194e42 kg are not fixed by the datum. (ii) The epoch is J2016.0: the radial approach moves the distance by -1.89e-4 relative to 2026.74 (4.2457 ly today), about 2.9 formal sigma, so the value holds as 'the J2016.0 barycentric distance', not as 'the distance'. (iii) The zero-point is uncorrected and the official recipe is invalid at Proxima's colour, so the size of the systematic is OPEN at the few-1e-5 level. None of this is an error in Gaia, and none is WRONG in the tree: the tree's own arithmetic and its 'EXACTLY' (branelink.py:64-65) are correct as statements about the unit definition. The narrowing concerns the class of statements the value supports (~4 significant figures at a stated epoch), not the tree's conclusions.
what_would_change_the_grade: -> STANDS: if the tree recorded the parallax, its sigma (+-0.00028 ly) and the J2016.0 epoch at foliation.py:583 / nonstatic.py:257 and stopped claiming 5-figure physical precision downstream, the use would match the source's hypotheses. -> DATA-DEPENDENT: only if a conclusion came to rest on the 4th-5th figure (none does now), or if Gaia DR4 or another independent parallax differed from DR3 by far more than the 6e-4 spread seen so far. -> WRONG: nothing READ here supports it; it would need an independent parallax off by a large fraction, which HST 2025 excludes at <0.1%. -> OPEN on the zero-point component alone until a validated bias estimate for nu_eff < 1.24 bright stars (or DR4) is READ.
